hypotheses.construction_plan: Define K(a,b)=T(a,b). Apply the S2 symmetrization operator to K to form Sym_S2[K](a,b)=K(a,b)+K(b,a). Specialize a to i and b to j to obtain the raw expression.
required_assumptions: T is defined on the ordered pairs (i,j) and (j,i).
hypotheses.rationale: The raw expression is exactly the sum over the two orderings of a two-slot kernel, so its visible structure is S2-symmetrization.

hypotheses.construction_plan: Evaluate the master two-argument kernel K at (a,b)=(i,j). The identity evaluation gives T(i,j), while the slot permutation gives T(j,i). Summing the two instantiations reconstructs the raw expression.
required_assumptions: The two terms are admissible evaluations of a common two-argument kernel under argument order reversal.
hypotheses.rationale: The two non-identical subexpressions are evaluations of a single ordered kernel with exchanged arguments, which directly explains the pair of terms in the raw expression.
